NYCHA residential addresses

Source: R/data.R
nyc_addresses_df.Rd

All residential addresses associated with NYCHA developments, including building, stairhall, and tax-lot identifiers, plus geographic and administrative boundary information.

Usage

nyc_addresses_df

Format

nyc_addresses_df

A tibble with 2,955 rows and 27 columns:

development

Development name.

tds_num

Tenant Data System (TDS) development number.

building_num

Building number within development.

stairhall_num

Stairhall number within building.

borough

New York City borough (title case).

house_num

Street number portion of the address.

street

Street name.

address

Full street address.

city

Postal city (typically Bronx, Brooklyn, New York, etc.).

state

State (NY).

zip_code

Five-digit ZIP code, e.g. "10456" (character).

bin

Building Identification Number (BIN), Department of City Planning.

block

Tax block.

lot

Tax lot (character).

bbl

Borough-block-lot identifier (10-digit concatenation).

census_tract_2020

2020 census tract as given in the source (character). The source uses two encodings. A whole tract has its label, e.g. "145" for tract 145. A split tract has its six-digit tract code without the leading zero, e.g. "15101" for tract 151.01. Use tract_geoid to join to census data.

tract_geoid

11-digit 2020 census tract GEOID (state, county, and tract), e.g. "36005014500" (character). Assigned from latitude and longitude with nycmaps::nyc_census_tracts_2020_sf.

nta_code

2020 Neighborhood Tabulation Area code.

nta_name

2020 Neighborhood Tabulation Area name.

community_district

Community District.

city_council_district

New York City Council district.

state_assembly_district

New York State Assembly district.

state_senate_district

New York State Senate district.

us_congressional_district

U.S. Congressional district.

privately_managed

TRUE if the property is privately managed under the Rental Assistance Demonstration (RAD/PACT), otherwise FALSE (logical).

latitude

Latitude (WGS 84).

longitude

Longitude (WGS 84).

Source

NYC OpenData: https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Housing-Development/NYCHA-Residential-Addresses/k6ya-3sk4

Details

The NYC Open Data export formats some identifier fields with thousands separators, e.g. ZIP code "10,456". The separators are removed.

The coordinates are address points at the building frontage: the median distance to the building footprint with the same BIN is about 3 feet. Other geocoders place the same addresses differently. 311 service requests (nyc311) are geocoded to the street centerline: for 311 requests at NYCHA addresses in 2022-2025, the 311 point is a median of 26 m from the building, and about 100 m at the 90th percentile, because many NYCHA buildings are set back from the street in superblocks. Distance joins to these points, and point-in-polygon joins to nyc_developments_sf, miss most such records.

To match other data to NYCHA addresses, join on bbl (nyc311 has it from version 0.0.3.9000, nycpluto throughout), or on bin where the other data have it. Matching on zip_code and a normalized address (upper case, ordinal suffixes dropped, so "12TH STREET" becomes "12 STREET") also works, but finds about 10% fewer 311 requests than bbl.
